key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A62
name: signed_divide_32_software
description: Software signed 32-bit division, needed because the 68000 has no full 32-by-32 divide. Negative operands are negated and the routine re-enters itself; positive operands are normalized and a trial quotient is corrected, with a fast path for 16-bit divisors that returns a remainder.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A68
name: draw_inset_panel
description: Draws a 48-by-16 panel whose origin is inset by three units from the given coordinates, storing that position and the requested fill value in game state, then passes it to a graphics-library drawing call. When the stack-space check fails it calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character instead.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A6E
name: draw_bordered_frame
description: Draws a rectangular frame from the given position and size as a series of line segments in the current pen colour, with inner edges offset by one to three units. A closing call with fixed arguments follows; when stack space is exhausted it calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A74
name: read_grid_cell
description: Reads a byte from a grid table of 25 entries per column at the given column and row. When that byte equals 1 it adds the results of two calls to a routine made with fixed arguments before returning the total.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A7A
name: run_fixed_call_sequence
description: Makes four calls to a routine with small fixed arguments in a set order and returns the result of the last one. The stack-exhaustion path calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A80
name: call_graphics_move_entry
description: Jumps through the graphics library base to its Move entry, which sets the drawing pen position.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A86
name: call_add_gadget_list
description: Jumps through the library base to its AddGList entry, which attaches a gadget list to a window.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A8C
name: call_set_pen_colour
description: Jumps through the graphics library base to its SetAPen entry, which sets the foreground pen used for later drawing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A92
name: pass_global_block_and_return
description: Passes the address of a global data block to one routine, then returns the result of a second routine called on a value stored in global data. The stack-exhaustion path calls a fixed message routine instead.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A98
name: add_when_below_limit
description: Returns the first argument, increased by a value from a routine, when it is below the second argument; otherwise returns it unchanged. The stack-exhaustion path calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1A9E
name: select_mode_and_store
description: Accepts a mode of 0 or 1. For a valid mode it stores the mode in a global and returns the result of a routine called with that mode; otherwise it returns one.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AA4
name: read_record_byte_four
description: Returns the byte at offset 4 of a record whose pointer is kept in global data.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AAA
name: walk_node_list_flags
description: Walks a linked list starting from a pointer in global data, reading each node's flag word and a 16-bit field. It passes each node to a routine, and when the flag bit with value 1024 is set it also passes the 16-bit field.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AB0
name: map_level_through_table
description: Maps an input level to an output value through a small four-entry lookup table, using two values from a routine as bounds. If no entry matches it returns a default kept in global data.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AB6
name: take_budget_if_available
description: Subtracts a requested amount from a global budget counter and returns true when enough remains. Otherwise it calls a routine with zero and returns false.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1ABC
name: dispatch_numbered_library_request
description: Maps a request code from 0 to 9 to one of ten library calls, each with its own fixed size or address constant, and returns the call's result. Codes outside that range are passed to a default routine.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AC2
name: draw_wrapped_text_lines
description: Draws a string line by line, measuring each line's length, padding according to a mode of 1 or 2, and handling newline characters. It tracks the column in a text-state record and wraps when a line exceeds the record's width.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AC8
name: dispatch_selector_nine
description: Calls a routine with selector nine followed by the two arguments it receives and returns the result. The stack-exhaustion path calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1ACE
name: refresh_unset_entries
description: Calls a routine with fixed arguments, then calls another routine with the index of each of eight slots whose flag is clear, followed by seventeen further indexed entries whose flag is clear. It finishes with a call using a saved value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AD4
name: unsigned_divide_32_quot_rem
description: Unsigned 32-by-32 software division returning a 64-bit pair of quotient and remainder, needed because the 68000 has no full 32-bit divide. It normalizes the divisor and corrects an estimated quotient.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1ADA
name: call_remove_gadget
description: Jumps through the library base to its RemoveGadget entry, which detaches a gadget from a window.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AE0
name: release_display_resources
description: Resets several display-state bytes, then frees each non-null resource pointer held in global data by calling a routine on it and clearing the pointer. It finishes with one more release call and a closing routine that returns a value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AE6
name: multiply_32_low_halves
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from their 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product, because the 68000 has no full 32-bit multiply.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AEC
name: select_by_threshold_table
description: Chooses one of six global entries according to whether the argument is below 10, 20, 50, 100 or 500, and passes the chosen entry's address to a routine. Values of 500 or more use the last entry.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AF2
name: draw_clamped_value_bars
description: Sets a colour from global data and issues a fixed graphics call with the arguments 24, 256 and 158. It then uses two computed values, capped at 13, to make two further calls before returning a stored value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AF8
name: emit_selected_text_entry
description: When a mode byte is non-zero, selects one of two strings by a 16-bit setting, writes it through a text routine, and returns the result of a routine applied to the mode. Otherwise it returns zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1AFE
name: store_byte_and_dispatch
description: Stores its argument in byte 7 of a record, calls two routines through global pointers with that argument, and returns the second routine's result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B04
name: reload_five_slot_table
description: Releases each non-null entry of a five-slot pointer table, then refills the table from five bytes in global data, calling a routine for each byte below 25. It returns the count five.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B0A
name: lookup_indexed_global_entry
description: Calls a routine with a fixed global address, then returns the result of a routine applied to the entry of a pointer table selected by the byte argument.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B10
name: handle_text_character
description: Processes one character code for text output. Code 256 redraws a bordered area from record fields and resets the position; carriage return and line feed reset the column, and line feed also advances the row. Any other code is drawn and advances the column, wrapping when the record width is exceeded.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B16
name: set_mode_and_select_palette
description: Calls a library routine with the argument 255, then returns the result of a routine applied to a global byte. It stores 23 in a global when the flag is zero and 5 otherwise.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B1C
name: call_set_draw_mode
description: Jumps through the graphics library base to its SetDrMd entry, which sets the drawing mode for later rendering.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B22
name: wait_for_key_in_range
description: Reads input characters until it gets a return or escape code, or a character lying between the two bounds passed in, and returns that character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B28
name: call_remove_gadget_list
description: Jumps through the graphics library base to its RemoveGList entry, which detaches a gadget list from a window.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B2E
name: draw_option_marker
description: Sets up drawing state, then draws a marker of size 13 at one of two fixed positions chosen by the argument (horizontal 112 or 203, vertical 172), and returns the result of a final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B34
name: set_cursor_bytes
description: Stores its first argument in one byte of a text-state record and a second value in the next byte. When the flag is non-zero the second value is reduced by the record's first byte, and that first byte is returned; otherwise zero is returned.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B3A
name: init_layout_constants
description: Writes a fixed set of 16-bit layout constants into global data when the argument is zero, then calls routines using them. The other argument case is handled by a separate branch of the same routine.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B40
name: draw_two_fixed_boxes
description: Draws two 48-by-16 boxes at fixed positions on the same row, then issues a call on a global record with fixed arguments and returns its result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B46
name: compute_offset_and_call
description: Calls a routine with the argument, stores its result, then calls another routine with the fixed value 16 and that result and returns that second result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B4C
name: call_text_render_entry
description: Jumps through the graphics library base to its Text entry, which draws a string at the current pen position.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B52
name: reset_view_and_draw_region
description: Clears a record byte, makes several routine calls using values from global data and a table, and fills a 303-by-16 rectangle at fixed coordinates. It finishes with two calls and returns the result of the last one.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B58
name: select_region_width_and_draw
description: Makes one routine call with a fixed argument, then draws a region 68 units high at a fixed origin. Its width is 240 when the argument is zero and 288 otherwise.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B5E
name: wait_until_value_matches
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns the given value, then makes one more call when that value is odd.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B64
name: forward_three_arg_call
description: Forwards its three arguments to one routine and returns that routine's result. The stack-exhaustion path calls a fixed message routine and returns an upper-cased character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B6A
name: redraw_selection_panel
description: Resets flags and calls several routines. When the argument is non-zero it releases two cached resources, creates a new one from the argument, draws with it and releases it. It then draws the panel at one of two widths depending on the arguments and finishes with a call on a global byte.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B70
name: multiply_32_low_halves
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from their 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product, because the 68000 has no full 32-bit multiply.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B76
name: uppercase_character
description: Converts a lower-case ASCII letter to upper case by subtracting 32. Other values are returned unchanged.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B7C
name: draw_capped_number
description: Draws a number with a field width of 32. Values above 999 are first reduced through a routine, and in that case a fixed follow-up call with the value 75 is made.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:4:1B82
name: draw_three_option_labels
description: Draws three labels at fixed vertical positions 20, 21 and 22 in a 256-wide column, each offset by the argument when its flag is set, with fixed extra sizes of 22, 56 and 90. It returns the result of the last draw call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:28:0028
name: jump_to_close_window
description: Jumps through the library base to its CloseWindow entry, which closes a window.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:28:003C
name: jump_to_close_workbench
description: Jumps through the library base to its CloseWorkBench entry, which closes the Workbench screen.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:28:0064
name: jump_to_display_beep
description: Jumps through the library base to its DisplayBeep entry, which signals the user with a screen beep.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:28:0078
name: jump_to_get_prefs
description: Jumps through the library base to its GetPrefs entry, which reads system preference settings.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:28:00F0
name: jump_to_open_screen
description: Jumps through the library base to its OpenScreen entry, which opens a new screen.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:27:0034
name: jump_to_close_font
description: Jumps through the library base to its CloseFont entry, which releases a font.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:27:0048
name: jump_to_load_rgb4
description: Jumps through the library base to its LoadRGB4 entry, which loads a colour palette of 4-bit components.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:27:0064
name: jump_to_init_rastport
description: Jumps through the library base to its InitRastPort entry, which initialises a drawing rastport.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:27:0078
name: jump_to_wait_blit
description: Jumps through the library base to its WaitBlit entry, which waits for the blitter to finish.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:27:0154
name: jump_to_init_bitmap
description: Jumps through the library base to its InitBitMap entry, which initialises a bitmap structure.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:25:0000
name: jump_to_lock
description: Jumps through the library base to its Lock entry, which locks a file or directory name for access.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:25:001C
name: jump_to_unlock
description: Jumps through the library base to its UnLock entry, which releases a lock on a file or directory.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:25:0030
name: jump_to_examine
description: Jumps through the library base to its Examine entry, which fills a structure describing a locked file or directory.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:25:007C
name: jump_to_delay
description: Jumps through the library base to its Delay entry, which pauses execution for a period of time.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:0000
name: jump_to_forbid
description: Jumps through the library base to its Forbid entry, which disables task switching until it is re-enabled.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:0038
name: jump_to_deallocate
description: Jumps through the library base to its Deallocate entry, which returns a block of memory to a pool.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:0054
name: jump_to_alloc_mem
description: Jumps through the library base to its AllocMem entry, which allocates a block of memory.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:006C
name: jump_to_free_mem
description: Jumps through the library base to its FreeMem entry, which returns a block of memory to the system.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:00E8
name: jump_to_close_library
description: Jumps through the library base to its CloseLibrary entry, which releases a library opened earlier.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:26:016C
name: jump_to_open_library
description: Jumps through the library base to its OpenLibrary entry, which opens a named shared library.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:libs/icon.library:0:00DC

name: mark_object_for_deferred_free

name: forward_no_arg_stub
